categories.main_business_segments: Sumitomo Warehouse Co., Ltd. operates two main business segments: logistics and real estate. The logistics segment encompasses warehousing, port transportation, international freight forwarding, and land transportation, while the real estate segment focuses on the leasing, sale, and management of office buildings and land.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced logistics management, including digital transformation (DX), automation in warehouses, and integrated multimodal transport solutions (land, sea, air). It also utilizes earthquake-resistant construction methods for storage facilities and implements ISO-certified quality and security management systems.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Sumitomo Warehouse serves a broad range of customers, including manufacturers (automotive, metals, chemicals), trading companies, retailers (including e-commerce), and other logistics providers. Its services are essential for industries requiring reliable storage, transportation, and supply chain solutions both domestically and internationally.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in Japan, with significant logistics and real estate assets in major cities such as Osaka, Tokyo, Kobe, Yokohama, and Nagoya. Internationally, it has subsidiaries and operations in the United States, Europe (notably Germany and Belgium), China, Singapore, Thailand, and Hong Kong, supporting a global logistics network.
categories.supply_chain_position: Sumitomo Warehouse is positioned as a midstream and downstream logistics provider, acting as a key integrator and facilitator between manufacturers, importers/exporters, and end-users by offering storage, handling, and transportation services across the supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include expanding domestic and overseas logistics bases, advancing digital transformation (DX) and automation, enhancing value-added logistics services, and strengthening ESG initiatives such as greenhouse gas reduction and human capital investment. The company is also focused on sustainable growth and resilience against climate change and supply chain disruptions.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through service fees for warehousing, transportation (port, land, international), and value-added logistics services, as well as rental income from real estate leasing. Additional revenue streams include software development and related logistics IT services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Sumitomo Warehouse is a leading Japanese logistics and real estate company, competing with other major domestic and international logistics providers such as Mitsui-Soko, Nippon Express, and Kintetsu World Express. It differentiates itself through its integrated service offering, long-standing reputation, and strong asset base.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated operating revenue was ¥193.4 billion, with operating profit of ¥13.3 billion and net profit attributable to shareholders of ¥20.1 billion. The company has shown stable growth in logistics revenue, with a strong balance sheet (total assets ¥439.8 billion) and a workforce of approximately 4,450 employees.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Sumitomo Warehouse emphasizes reliability, safety, and high-quality logistics solutions backed by over 120 years of experience. Its value proposition includes comprehensive, integrated logistics services, robust risk management, advanced digital and automation capabilities, and a commitment to sustainability and customer-centric innovation.
